notes:
disagreement: value: the kind of the requirement that the service uses the permanent criteria: one pass writes create, the other change; chose change, since the cell is set by a later update call on the service created earlier in the task (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the validation task's short_description: one pass requires the benchmark's exact text 'Final Compensation Review Validation for High Priority Case.', the other only that it contain 'Final Compensation Review Validation'; chose the exact text, since it is built from the request's words and nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts it, so the task check is repaired only by dropping its server-assigned number (resolved on that requirement).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition: topic detail 36 under Benefits (3), the two criteria selected by name (groups 10 and 6), service 55, rule 9, user skill 336, member 44, case 61, task 150 and checklist item 91; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
Seed task titles are bare names (for example 'Add Beneficiaries'); an agent that titles the task 'Final Compensation Review Validation' alone fails the task requirement.
No benchmark check tests the test case itself, so a new requirement covers it (hr_case 61, the parent the task check already assumes). The Payroll skill attached to that case goes in the skills JSON column, which is null on every seed case, so its storage format is not shown and the cell is left out as untestable.
The case short description would follow only the policy's 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: .' template; no benchmark check tests it and the request gives no text, so it is not a cell.
The Compensation Inquiry service is first created with the temporary criteria and then moved to the permanent one; only the final reference can be tested. The temporary criteria stays active, as the benchmark tests and the request does not say to deactivate it.
The routing rule adds a based_on_skills cell the benchmark omits: the request says the rule routes cases requiring the Payroll skill, and every seed rule stores skill names as a JSON list of strings; an agent that stores the skill id instead would fail that cell.
The acting user, Joanne Simpson (user 4), holds the manager role in org 1. The policy reserves services, assignment rules and other system configuration for administrators, but the seed's permission table grants the manager role create, read, update and delete on topic details, criteria, services, skills, groups and assignment rules, and the request asks for each step explicitly, so the configuration steps are required.
